name: Self-Improving Collodion Baby

criteria.description: Presence of a taut, shiny, parchment-like collodion membrane at birth
Spontaneous shedding of the collodion membrane with near-complete skin normalization within the first few weeks of life
Lack of persistent ichthyosis or other severe skin abnormalities after membrane shedding
Exclusion of other hereditary ichthyoses or syndromic conditions by clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of collodion membrane at birth with spontaneous resolution and absence of persistent ichthyosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may be used to exclude other ichthyoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Collodion membrane covering entire body surface at birth
searchTerms: tight membrane over entire baby at birth
collodion membrane present on newborn skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Spontaneous desquamation of collodion membrane within 2-4 weeks
searchTerms: peeling off of skin membrane within weeks
skin feels tight and stretched all over

common.symptomName: Mild dehydration due to increased transepidermal water loss
searchTerms: mild dehydration from water loss through skin
dryness due to increased skin water loss
loss of body fluids from skin evaporation
temporary low body temperature in newborn

occasional.symptomName: Mild scaling or xerosis after membrane shedding
searchTerms: mild flaky or dry skin after birth

rare.symptomName: Transient mild respiratory distress due to restrictive skin
searchTerms: temporary mild breathing difficulty due to tight skin
short-term breathing trouble from skin tightness

rare.symptomName: Mild electrolyte imbalance secondary to dehydration
searchTerms: electrolyte changes due to fluid loss

rare.symptomName: Transient feeding difficulties in neonatal period

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests except possible mild dehydration markers
Normal electrolyte panel or mild transient imbalances
imaging: Not typically required; chest imaging if respiratory distress suspected
other: Clinical observation of membrane shedding and skin normalization

distinguishingFeatures: Persistent scaling and hyperkeratosis after birth
No spontaneous resolution of collodion membrane
High neonatal mortality without rapid intervention

redFlags: Failure of collodion membrane to shed within 4 weeks
Development of persistent ichthyosis or erythroderma after membrane shedding
Signs of systemic infection or severe dehydration
references: Griffiths WA, et al. Self-improving collodion baby: clinical and genetic aspects. Dermatol Clin. 2010;28(4):603-610.
Rajpopat S, et al. Clinical and genetic characterization of self-improving collodion ichthyosis. J Invest Dermatol. 2013;133(3):742-745.
